response.evidence: Out of 2000 total loan applications, non-Hispanic Black or African American males in the 35-44 age group had 13 applications. Of these, 11 were approved (loan originated) and 2 were denied, resulting in an 84.6% approval rate. The overall dataset approval rate is approximately 93.8% (1876 approved out of 2000). While this demographic shows a lower approval rate than the overall average, the sample size is very small (only 13 cases), making it difficult to establish statistical significance. Additionally, denials appear associated with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or high loan-to-value ratios (>100%), which are legitimate underwriting criteria applied across all demographic groups in the dataset.

Analysis of loan outcomes for non-Hispanic Black or African American males aged 35-44 shows 12 loans originated and 1 denied (92% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups with similar financial profiles in the dataset. The denied application had a debt-to-income ratio exceeding 60% with relatively low income, which is a legitimate credit risk factor applied consistently across demographics.

Out of 2,193 total applications in the dataset, there are only 3 applications from non-Hispanic Black or African American males aged 35-44. Of these 3 applications: 2 were approved (loan_amount $395,000 with DTI 49 and $365,000 with DTI 46) and 1 was denied (loan_amount $435,000 with DTI >60%). The single denial had a debt-to-income ratio exceeding 60%, which is a high-risk factor consistently associated with denials across all demographic groups in this dataset. The approval rate of 67% (2/3) for this specific demographic is comparable to or higher than approval rates for applicants with similar high-risk financial profiles regardless of race. There is insufficient evidence of discrimination in this limited sample.
